title: Fishtail (Fell) projectile point complex of South America
summary: Fishtail or Fell points, named for Fell’s Cave in Patagonia, are broad, thin and often fluted stone projectile points. They appear from about 13,000 to 11,000 years ago across South America, densest in the Southern Cone, and are linked to hunting of now-extinct large animals.

uncertainty.note: 13–11 k cal BP converted as 1950 minus cal BP. Redating of Fell’s Cave hearths gives about 10,850 to 10,300 radiocarbon years BP (12,800 to 12,100 cal BP) for the type there.

where.modern_name: Fell’s Cave, southern Chile (type site; points occur across South America)

importance.justification: The earliest widespread projectile type in South America, tied to megafauna hunting and the peopling of the continent.

sources.title: Changes in projectile design and size of prey reveal the central role of Fishtail points in megafauna hunting in South America
sources.author: Prates et al.

sources.title: Redating Fell’s Cave, Chile and the Chronological Placement of the Fishtail Projectile Point

reviewer_note: The id says 13 ka but the cal BP range runs 13–11 ka; the pin is the type site only, since the complex spans a continent (uncertainty_km is nominal). Wikidata coordinates for Fell’s Cave are rounded.
